key_insight: ContiLNN adds bidirectional liquid neural-network modules to standard 2D restoration models so they can use cross-slice anatomy while better handling irregular slice spacing.
clinical_relevance: This could improve medical image restoration quality for CT, MRI, and PET, which may support clearer images for downstream interpretation and analysis.
method: Adds Bi-CfC modules for bidirectional cross-slice propagation.
Uses slice-interval-aware gating driven by local features and hidden states.
Adds consistency loss plus distillation from a frozen backbone to preserve in-plane detail.
evidence_signal: Across five training seeds, ContiLNN improved mean PSNR over Restore-RWKV on CT denoising, MRI super-resolution, and reduced-count PET restoration, with lower RMSE in all three tasks.
watch_item: Reported gains are strongest in benchmark settings, and CT results are described for one held-out patient, so real-world generalization and deployment performance still need careful validation.
paper_title: ContiLNN: Mitigating Slice Sampling Discontinuity with Liquid Neural Networks for Medical Image Restoration
